pride_data.title: The ULK1 effector BAG2 regulates autophagy initiation by modulating AMBRA1 localization
pride_data.projectDescription: In this projectby two sets of interaction-proteomic experiments were performed: (1) miniTURBO proximity labeling (PL) of ULK1 complex members ULK1, ATG13, ATG101 and RB1CC1/FIP200; and (2) anti-HA affinity purification (AP) of ULK1 complex members ULK1, ATG13, ATG101 and RB1CC1/FIP200
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Each comparison was performed in biological triplicates giving rise to a total of 24 AP- and 24 PL-MS studies of ULK1 complex members, plus 24 negative controls. Experiments were performed using triple SILAC labeling, in each experiment comparing N- and C-terminal tagged proteins of interest against HA-miniTURBO-GFP negative controls, the negative control always being in light label (0/0). Purifications were fractioned by SDS-PAGE, lanes cut into 5 slices per experiment and proteins in gel-digested by trypsin, giving rise to 60 LC-MSMS measurements per experimental group.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: MaxQuant software (version 1.6.2.10) (Cox and Mann, 2008) was used for analyzing the MS raw files for peak detection, peptide quantification and identification using full length Uniprot human databases (version April 2016/ Jan 2022) and common contaminants. Carbamidomethylcysteine was used as fixed modification and N-terminal acetylation, oxidation of methionine, and in case of phosphorylation site analyses phosphorylation of serine, threonine or tyrosine were set as variable modifications. The MS/MS tolerance was set to 20 ppm and four missed cleavages were allowed for Trypsin/P as enzyme specificity. Based on a forward-reverse database, protein and peptide FDR was set to 0.01, minimum peptide length was set to seven, and at least one unique peptide had to be identified. The match-between run option was set to 0.7 minutes.
